title: Produce a Consolidated Story Analysis Run Report

story.so_that: certification evidence and workflow reliability can be reviewed without reconstructing runs from scattered logs
story.i_want: each terminal workflow run summarized in one structured report and included in an auditable success-rate aggregate

target_persona.name: Story Analysis Workflow Certification Owner
target_persona.role: Certification owner responsible for workflow evidence and reliability metrics

journey.before: Reviews terminal workflow runs, activity logs, ATIF usage exports, and outcome annotations to understand how each run completed.
journey.during: Inspects a consolidated per-run report and an aggregate success-rate metric that includes status counts, formula, sample window, and manual-intervention count.
journey.after: Presents auditable run evidence and reproducible success metrics to certification examiners without reconstructing runs from scattered logs.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Produce one schema-versioned report for each terminal Story Analysis Workflow run and aggregate visible reports into auditable success-rate metrics
inputs: Terminal workflow run metadata (workflow_id, run_id, story_document, final_status, attempt_count, terminal outcome origin)
Executed activity attempt records (step name, activity type, attempt, model, permission mode, duration, output path)
cost_usd when supplied by the supported usage source
Collection of visible terminal-run reports for aggregation
Certification-owner decision on sample window, success formula, and threshold
outputs: Success-rate aggregate with status counts, formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count
Explicit unavailable cost representation when cost_usd is absent
state_changes: A terminal run becomes auditable from a single report file
A collection of reports yields a reproducible end-to-end success metric
Cost fields are marked unavailable rather than estimated when absent
side_effects: Workflow log emits report-written and aggregation-published events
Raw ATIF trajectory files remain in their original activity artifact directories
Aggregates are published alongside the reports they consume for traceability

ui: Workflow CLI status/query output may expose report_path and final_status
Certification review tooling reads {workflow}.report.json and aggregate JSON
api: src/story_analysis_workflow/workflow.py: workflow result contract and completion
src/common/skill_activity.py: SkillActivityOutput extension to carry attempt, model, permission_mode, duration, and output_path
src/common/atif_usage.py: read_atif_usage_result for normalized token and cost data
src/common/workflow_logger.py: get_activity_artifact_dir and activity attempt-scoped log layout
New report writer module and report JSON Schema
New aggregation module and success-rate query/starter support
database: No application database schema change is required
Cadence persistence stores WorkflowExecution Event History
Filesystem report and log artifacts require deterministic paths
external_services: Host filesystem for report and trajectory storage

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a workflow reaches a terminal state, when completion processing finishes, then exactly one schema-valid report exists for its workflow_id and run_id.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow reaches a terminal state When completion processing finishes Then exactly one schema-valid {workflow}.report.json exists for its workflow_id and run_id
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Obtain one auditable report per workflow run

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a run contains retries, when the report is read, then every activity attempt appears once in execution order and retry attempts are not collapsed or double-counted.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a run contains activity retries When the report is read Then every activity attempt appears once in execution order and retries are not collapsed or double-counted
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Inspect every activity attempt in execution order

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given usage metrics are available in ATIF, when the report is written, then prompt, completion, and cached token totals match the source data and the raw ATIF artifact remains available.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given usage metrics are available in ATIF When the report is written Then prompt, completion, and cached token totals match the source data and the raw ATIF artifact remains available
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Trust token usage totals from the raw ATIF artifact

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given cost_usd is absent from ATIF, when the report is written, then cost is explicitly unavailable and no estimated value is invented.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given cost_usd is absent from ATIF When the report is written Then cost is explicitly unavailable and no estimated value is invented

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the run ends through automated failure, human accept, or human abort, when the report is read, then the final status and outcome origin distinguish those paths.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the run ends through automated failure, human accept, or human abort When the report is read Then the final status and outcome origin distinguish those terminal paths
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Distinguish how each run was resolved

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given report generation is interrupted, when evidence is inspected, then no truncated report is accepted as complete and rerunning completion for the same run produces one valid result.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given report generation is interrupted When evidence is inspected Then no truncated report is accepted as complete and rerunning completion for the same run produces one valid result

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given concurrent workflows and activity retries, when their reports are generated, then records remain isolated by workflow, run, activity, and attempt.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given concurrent workflows and activity retries When their reports are generated Then records remain isolated by workflow, run, activity, and attempt

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a set of visible reports, when aggregation runs, then it publishes status counts, the defined success formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count, with each observation traceable to one report.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a set of visible reports When aggregation runs Then it publishes status counts, the defined success formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count with each observation traceable to one report

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given retries occur within a run, when the success rate is calculated, then the run contributes at most one observation to the denominator.

edge_cases.criterion: Workflow metadata is missing one or more required fields
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a terminal run is missing workflow_id, run_id, story_document, final_status, or attempt_count When the report writer runs Then it emits a validation error and does not produce a schema-invalid report

edge_cases.criterion: No activity attempts were executed before terminal status
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a run reaches a terminal state without any recorded activity attempts When the report is generated Then the attempts array is empty and the final status still has a clear outcome origin
edge_cases.jtbd: Handle a run with no activity attempts

edge_cases.criterion: ATIF export is missing, unreadable, or contains invalid JSON
edge_cases.gherkin: Given an activity attempt has no readable ATIF export When the report is written Then token and cost fields for that attempt are explicitly unavailable and the raw path is omitted
edge_cases.jtbd: Tolerate missing or malformed ATIF exports

edge_cases.criterion: ATIF final_metrics is missing some supported fields
edge_cases.gherkin: Given ATIF final_metrics provides only prompt_tokens and cached_tokens When the report is written Then completion_tokens and cost_usd are explicitly unavailable while available fields are recorded

edge_cases.criterion: Token or cost fields have wrong types or negative values
edge_cases.gherkin: Given ATIF final_metrics contains a string, boolean, or negative number for a token or cost field When the report is written Then that field is marked unavailable and the rest of the report remains valid

edge_cases.criterion: Report write is interrupted before completion
edge_cases.gherkin: Given report generation is interrupted after the file is opened but before it is closed When the workflow is inspected or rerun Then the partial file is not accepted and regeneration produces exactly one valid report
edge_cases.jtbd: Avoid treating a partial report as complete

edge_cases.criterion: Report or log destination is unwritable
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the configured report path or log directory rejects a write When report generation runs Then the failure is logged and the run is not reported as complete

edge_cases.criterion: Concurrent workflows and activity retries write reports
edge_cases.gherkin: Given multiple workflow runs and activity retries execute concurrently When reports are generated Then each report is scoped to one workflow_id and run_id with no overwrites or mixed attempts
Given a run reaches the configured maximum grade-repair attempts When the report is written Then attempt_count reflects the bounded count and no additional repair is recorded

edge_cases.criterion: Human signal timeout with no decision
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a workflow awaits a human signal and both escalation waits time out When the report is generated Then the final status is failed with origin automated_timeout and the manual-intervention count is not incremented

edge_cases.criterion: Aggregation is asked over an empty or single-report sample
edge_cases.gherkin: Given zero or one visible terminal reports When aggregation runs Then the result still publishes the formula, sample window, and status counts with denominator equal to the sample size
edge_cases.jtbd: Aggregate over small or empty samples

edge_cases.criterion: Report files from mixed workflow versions or schemas
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a set of visible reports contains different schema versions When aggregation runs Then incompatible reports are either filtered or migrated and the sample window and count are reported accurately
edge_cases.jtbd: Handle schema drift in historical reports

edge_cases.criterion: Workflow or run identifiers contain path-unsafe characters
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a workflow_id or run_id contains slashes, dots, unicode, or spaces When the report path is derived Then the components are sanitized to prevent traversal and the report remains reachable
edge_cases.jtbd: Sanitize identifiers used as filesystem paths

recommendation.approach: Implement in this order: (1) define and version the {workflow}.report.json schema and deterministic report storage path; (2) extend SkillActivityOutput or activity log to carry model, permission_mode, attempt, duration, and ATIF artifact path; (3) implement a defensive report writer that reads workflow metadata, activity attempt records, and ATIF usage, marking cost as unavailable when absent and writing atomically; (4) add report generation at terminal workflow completion in the engine/workflow; (5) implement a report aggregator that scans visible reports, computes status counts, the success formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, and manual-intervention count, with each observation traceable to one report; (6) add tests covering all terminal paths, missing usage, partial writes, retries, and concurrent runs.
recommendation.rationale: The workflow already produces per-activity ATIF exports, attempt-scoped logs, and terminal status. The remaining work is to collect those existing artifacts into one schema-valid report per run and to aggregate visible reports without counting retries as separate runs. Cost should not be fabricated when ATIF omits it. Report generation must be atomic and idempotent so interrupted writes do not produce corrupt evidence. The success formula and threshold are a certification-owner decision, so the implementation must keep them explicit and configurable.
